Dividends only India, £1 per share plus £1 manager each; shareholder may forgo with manager consent. Record total paid retirement marker then sweep remainder India to London.
grades.observed_answer: At Revenue, firms pay expenses before the Company, in initiative order (then other firms; ties by manager’s most windows and PM clockwise order). Expenses are £1 per charter ship plus the higher of firm share count or firm Value, paid from London and/or India treasuries. After expenses, dividends may be paid only from India: each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager, though with manager consent a shareholder can forgo payments on any number of shares. Record total actual cash paid out as the dividend marker. An active non-Hobnob firm paying nothing records zero; Hobnob keeps its previous marker. Sweep remaining India cash to London. If a firm cannot pay expenses, it dissolves unless rescued: shareholders go to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships return to shipyards, charter to family side, while workshops stay invested. Rescue can use emergency investments under normal share/workshop rules (even if the ten-share limit blocks new shares), pay expenses, discard remaining cash, and lower Value one per emergency investment; alternatively merge with one other firm, which must first pay its own expenses if not already paid and cover the failing firm’s shortfall.
grades.summary_evidence: Firm expenses, dividend funding/calculation and marker rules stated. Insolvency section gives dissolution destinations and rescue by emergency investment or one other firm.
